evidence.claim: A São Paulo court ordered Bolsonaro to pay R$100,000 in collective damages to journalists, citing his attacks and threats against the profession and saying they encouraged virtual and physical attacks on journalists.
evidence.title: Bolsonaro é condenado por dano moral coletivo a jornalistas
evidence.excerpt: A São Paulo court ordered Bolsonaro to pay R$100,000 in collective damages to journalists, citing his attacks and threats against the profession and saying they encouraged virtual and physical attacks on journalists.
evidence.source_locator: Lead paragraph quoting the judge's reasoning
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters is a strong independent wire service, and the report quotes the court's reasoning directly.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Bolsonaro's public rhetoric as president and candidate.
contrary_evidence: This is a civil judgment, not a criminal conviction.
The Planalto did not immediately comment in the report.

evidence.claim: Bolsonaro said he would respect the October election result only if the vote was 'clean and transparent', maintaining conditional language when asked whether he would accept an adverse result.
evidence.title: No JN, Bolsonaro diz que vai reconhecer resultado das eleições desde que "limpas e transparentes"
evidence.excerpt: Bolsonaro said he would respect the October election result only if the vote was 'clean and transparent', maintaining conditional language when asked whether he would accept an adverse result.
evidence.source_locator: Interview quotes in the first half of the article
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters directly reports Bolsonaro's own public statement in the campaign period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Bolsonaro statement in his capacity as incumbent and candidate.
contrary_evidence: This was a public promise, not proof that he later rejected the result.
He did not yet have the final vote outcome when he said it.

evidence.claim: Bolsonaro again raised unsupported fraud suspicions about the electronic voting system, declined to disclose a military report, and repeated claims that the urns were unauditable despite repeated TSE explanations.
evidence.title: Bolsonaro volta a questionar urna eletrônica e diz que análise está sendo feita pelas Forças Armadas
evidence.excerpt: Bolsonaro again raised unsupported fraud suspicions about the electronic voting system, declined to disclose a military report, and repeated claims that the urns were unauditable despite repeated TSE explanations.
evidence.source_locator: Interview quotes and TSE context in the body
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters captures Bolsonaro's repeated public statements and places them against the TSE's prior explanations and election-observer findings.
contrary_evidence: Observers and the TSE said they had found no fraud in Brazil's electronic voting system.
The military review was incomplete or undisclosed at the time of the report.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Brazil's securities regulator found it strange that the federal government insisted on nominees to Petrobras' board who had been vetoed by the company's governance process.
evidence.title: CVM estranha insistência de governo sobre conselheiros vetados, dizem fontes
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Brazil's securities regulator found it strange that the federal government insisted on nominees to Petrobras' board who had been vetoed by the company's governance process.
evidence.source_locator: Lead paragraph and quoted CVM language
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters is strong independent reporting and the article quotes the regulator's reaction to the nominations.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly tied to Bolsonaro's government because the Union, under his administration, was the controlling shareholder.
contrary_evidence: This is about governance pressure, not a proven personal payoff.
The board process itself still involved formal review mechanisms.

evidence.claim: Bolsonaro said he warned relatives about a possible search-and-seizure operation tied to allegations about family property purchases and said such a move would create a media scandal.
evidence.title: Bolsonaro diz que alertou parentes sobre possivel busca e apreensao relacionada a compra de imoveis
evidence.excerpt: Bolsonaro said he warned relatives about a possible search-and-seizure operation tied to allegations about family property purchases and said such a move would create a media scandal.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs and quoted live-stream remarks
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting based on Bolsonaro's own public remarks, with direct attribution but only self-report on the underlying allegation.
evidence.period_fit: direct 2022 conduct and response to scrutiny
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable because the warning and public framing came from Jair Bolsonaro; the underlying property-purchase allegation remains investigatory and family-linked rather than adjudicated as his personal wrongdoing.
contrary_evidence: Bolsonaro denied irregularities and said 'money current' does not prove cash payments.
The article reports allegations, not a court finding.

evidence.claim: Federal Police analysis of messages on Mauro Cid's phone suggested fractional deposits and withdrawals intended to pay personal bills of Bolsonaro's family and people close to Michelle Bolsonaro.
evidence.title: Federal Police Sees Suspicious Transactions in Bolsonaro's Office
evidence.excerpt: Federal Police analysis of messages on Mauro Cid's phone suggested fractional deposits and withdrawals intended to pay personal bills of Bolsonaro's family and people close to Michelle Bolsonaro.
evidence.source_locator: paragraphs summarizing the PF analysis and quoted presidential office response
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters-style reporting on a police investigation with specific facts, but still an allegation rather than a judicial finding.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct nexus to Jair Bolsonaro is plausible because the alleged transactions are tied to his office and family, but the source itself stops short of proving his personal order or benefit.
contrary_evidence: The presidential office denied irregularities and said the money came from Bolsonaro's private account.
The article says the matter was under investigation without accusation or confirmation.

evidence.claim: Jose Carlos Oliveira, a career INSS public servant, was sworn in as Minister of Work and Previdencia in the presence of Bolsonaro and said he would continue and strengthen existing INSS policies through automation and better service.
evidence.title: Jose Carlos Oliveira e o novo Ministro do Trabalho e Previdencia
evidence.excerpt: Jose Carlos Oliveira, a career INSS public servant, was sworn in as Minister of Work and Previdencia in the presence of Bolsonaro and said he would continue and strengthen existing INSS policies through automation and better service.
evidence.source_locator: headline, lead paragraph, and possession/continuity paragraphs
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official ministry notice of a sworn-in cabinet appointment with qualifications and policy intentions stated on the record.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable because Bolsonaro was present and Oliveira assumed office under his government; the source supports a professional rather than purely loyalist appointment, but it does not by itself show broader cabinet quality.
contrary_evidence: The page is an official self-description of continuity and competence, not an independent assessment of performance.
The page was only reachable as a search result snippet in this session, not as a full open page.
